title: Disagreeing while still hearing each other
meaning: You can explain a disagreement while hearing the personal meaning of each other’s response, without making these different parts of conversation cancel one another.
text: Conversation can hold more than a choice between agreement and objection. The Hermit in the physical position of your Vishuddha helps you explain a distinction made clear through reflection. Temperance in energy encourages you to combine understanding of personal experience with honesty about your own position. Temperance in emotions has another role: feeling that different responses can fit together. You may not share a judgement and still feel contact between you. This combination does not require turning two positions into one.

For example, you discuss a reply to a message that seemed too curt. You explain that you would have read it differently, while understanding why the absence of a greeting made it unpleasant. **You can hear a feeling without sharing the judgement**. Both details remain in the conversation: your reading and the greeting’s personal significance. The disagreement can stop dividing every remark into right and wrong. You find a shared subject without promising to perceive every future message identically.

Yet a considered distinction can become a careful formula spoken without real interest in the answer. “I understand, but” then sounds like polite preparation for an objection, and the feeling of contact disappears. Constructive Temperance helps keep both parts alive: your own reading and the personal meaning you heard. Their combination becomes evident through the conversation that follows, rather than only through a correctly formed sentence.
